microtheory.name: universal_coordination
microtheory.definition: L6 composition pattern — universal coordination across the substrate's layers. Composed of: cybernetic feedback at the system level (Wiener's universal feedback pattern), Ashby's law of requisite variety as the regulator-disturbance match invariant at SYSTEM scale (vs the subsystem scale of L3), second-order observation (the substrate observes itself observing), homeostasis as the steady-state attractor, circular causality between layers, Theorem-Root style universal coordination (Paper 1's intended top-level theorem), and bounded coordination latency. Each piece exists in other Mts (cybernetics_systems' Wiener + Ashby + von Foerster + Maturana-Varela autopoiesis; paper1 Theorem Root; control_systems' stability margins); this Mt names how they compose for the TOP layer that regulates everything below.

concepts.name: universal_coordination_pattern
concepts.definition: The composition pattern. The top of the runner design stack. Below: L1 data, L2 dispatch, L3 drives, L4 subsystems, L5 codegen, shared executable-memory. L6 coordinates ACROSS all of them — ensures that L2's dispatch decisions are consistent with L3's drives are consistent with L4's subsystem boundaries are consistent with L5's compile invariants. Realised through cybernetic feedback (every layer observes every other layer, via shared atomics + graph-resident snapshots) + Ashby's variety match at SYSTEM scale + second-order observation (substrate watches itself).

concepts.name: cybernetic_feedback_at_system_scale
concepts.definition: Component 1. Wiener's universal feedback pattern applied at the SYSTEM level — every layer's output becomes feedback for adjacent layers. L1's allocation rate feeds L2's dispatch policy; L2's hot counters feed L3's gain scheduler; L3's drives feed L4's subsystem weighting; L4's subsystem load feeds L5's compile priorities. The loop is closed not just within layers but ACROSS layers.

concepts.name: ashby_variety_match_at_system_scale
concepts.definition: Component 2. Ashby's law of requisite variety — but at the WHOLE-SUBSTRATE scale. The substrate's total regulator variety (sum across L2 dispatch + L3 controllers + L4 subsystem set + L5 codegen kinds) must equal or exceed the total disturbance variety (sum across environment + Γ mutations + workload churn + hardware events). Substrate analogue: the system-scale variety check no single layer can perform alone.

concepts.name: second_order_observation_of_substrate
concepts.definition: Component 3. von Foerster's second-order cybernetics: the observer is included in the system. The substrate observes itself observing — via dispatcher snapshots in the graph (commit 13b84a4), via graph-resident Γ (Axiom 3), via reflective tower (L5). Without second-order observation, the substrate can't reason about its own behavior — only about what it processes.

concepts.name: homeostasis_at_system_steady_state
concepts.definition: Component 4. The substrate as a whole maintains essential variables (overall load, drive balance, working-set fit, deadline-meet rate) within bounds despite environmental perturbation. Cannon + Wiener's homeostasis at SYSTEM scale. Failure mode: an essential variable leaves bounds + substrate enters a degraded regime (e.g. all reflexes deadline-missed + working set blown).

concepts.name: circular_causality_between_layers
concepts.definition: Component 5. Maruyama's mutual causality applied between substrate layers. L2 affects L3 affects L4 affects L2 (via subsystem load shifting dispatch priority). Linear causal chains miss this dynamic; mutual causality required for honest modelling.

concepts.name: theorem_root_universal_coordination_target
concepts.definition: Component 6. Paper 1's Theorem Root — the intended top-level universal coordination theorem. Currently sparse in Jabberwock's vocabulary (commit 27f4afb walk noted weak coverage). This Mt names Theorem Root as the formal target the substrate's coordination layer aims at, even when not fully proven.

concepts.name: bounded_coordination_latency
concepts.definition: Component 7. Coordination signals (epoch bumps, snapshot installs, cross-layer feedback) must propagate within a bounded latency. Otherwise the layers' decisions become decoupled in time + coherence breaks down. substrate's reference: coordination latency < L2's tick period (100µs). Larger latency → uncoordinated layers acting on stale views.

concepts.name: autopoietic_closure_at_system_scale
concepts.definition: Component 8. Maturana + Varela's autopoiesis applied at the substrate level: the substrate maintains its own organisation under perturbation. The 6 layers + shared together produce the substrate; the substrate's behaviour reproduces the conditions for the layers to keep functioning. Self-producing system.

concepts.name: essential_variables_with_viability_bounds
concepts.definition: Component 9. Ashby's essential variables: variables whose departure from bounds means substrate failure. Substrate's essential variables: deadline-meet rate (> 95%), working set fit (≤ L3 cache), gamma_epoch coherence (no torn reads), drive balance (no drive starved > N ticks). The substrate's coordination layer's job is to keep these in bounds.

concepts.name: viability_envelope_as_design_constraint
concepts.definition: Component 10. The convex hull of substrate states where all essential variables stay in bounds. Coordination's success criterion is keeping the trajectory inside the envelope. Outside the envelope, substrate may still operate but in degraded mode.

concepts.name: essential_variables_stay_in_bounds
concepts.definition: Invariant. The substrate's essential variables (deadline-meet rate, working set fit, epoch coherence, drive balance) stay within their viability bounds during nominal operation. Departure signals coordination failure — the substrate can degrade or recover, but the coordination layer must DETECT the departure and act.

concepts.name: every_layer_feeds_every_other_via_named_signal
concepts.definition: Invariant. Cross-layer feedback uses named signals (gamma_epoch, hot_counters, drive_state, subsystem_load, code_cache_pressure, executable_memory_pressure). No layer reads another layer's internals; coordination goes through the named surface. Otherwise coupling is implicit + coherence is unverifiable.

concepts.name: second_order_self_observation_is_complete
concepts.definition: Invariant. Every layer's runtime state is observable from within the substrate (as graph data per Axiom 3). No layer has hidden state. The substrate can answer 'what am I doing?' completely from graph introspection. Hidden state = blind spot = uncoordinable.

concepts.name: system_scale_variety_match_holds
concepts.definition: Invariant. Substrate's total regulator variety ≥ total disturbance variety. Computed by summing per-layer variety (or via a logarithmic bound per Ashby). Violation: substrate is structurally underregulated; some failure mode is uncovered.

concepts.name: coordination_latency_within_tick_period
concepts.definition: Invariant. Cross-layer coordination signals propagate within one L2 tick period (100µs default). Otherwise layers act on stale views of each other + composition becomes incoherent.

concepts.name: tradeoff_coordination_tightness
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: tight coordination (every layer reads every other every tick → high overhead, perfect coherence) vs loose coordination (layers act mostly independently with periodic syncs → low overhead, occasional incoherence). substrate picks tight for safety-critical paths (drive deadlines), loose for soft paths (background introspection).

concepts.name: tradeoff_essential_variable_count
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: many essential variables (rich viability concept, expensive to monitor) vs few (cheap to monitor, coarser viability). substrate picks 4 essential variables (deadline-meet rate, working set fit, epoch coherence, drive balance) — minimal complete set.

concepts.name: tradeoff_viability_envelope_shape
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: hard bounds (sharp envelope, clear violation, brittle near edges) vs soft bounds (smooth envelope, gradual degradation, harder to detect failure). substrate picks soft bounds with logged-on-near-edge events.

concepts.name: tradeoff_second_order_depth
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: substrate observing itself observing (level 2) is cheap; substrate observing itself observing itself observing (level 3+) is recursive cost vs introspection power. substrate picks 2 levels eager + lazy beyond (matches reflective_codegen_axiom3's tower_finite_with_lazy_depth).

concepts.name: tradeoff_when_to_invoke_coordination
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: continuous coordination (every tick → fine-grained but expensive) vs event-driven (on essential variable threshold cross → cheaper but reactive only). substrate picks hybrid: continuous summary (per-tick essential variable check), event-driven response (only on near-edge or violation).

concepts.name: substrate_rs_coordination_status
concepts.definition: substrate_rs as canonical. Some coordination already realised: gamma_epoch broadcasts (Axiom 3 + L5 invalidation), graph-resident dispatcher snapshots (commit 13b84a4 + l2_graph_bridge). Most coordination is NOT YET implemented — essential variables aren't monitored; system-scale variety isn't checked; viability envelope isn't enforced. The Mt names the design future work realises.

concepts.name: ashby_homeostat_reference
concepts.definition: Ashby's homeostat (1948). The historical predecessor: a physical device maintaining essential variables within bounds via mechanical feedback. Reference for essential_variables_with_viability_bounds + homeostasis_at_system_steady_state.

concepts.name: stafford_beer_viable_system_model_reference
concepts.definition: Stafford Beer's Viable System Model (1972). Organisations as 5-system cybernetic structures (operations + coordination + control + intelligence + identity). Closest organisational analogue to substrate's 6-layer-plus-shared. Reference for cross-layer coordination at system scale.

concepts.name: von_foerster_observing_systems_reference
concepts.definition: Heinz von Foerster's 'Observing Systems' (1981). Second-order cybernetics: the observer included in the system. Reference for second_order_observation_of_substrate. Theoretical foundation of why the substrate must include itself in its own observation surface.

concepts.name: maturana_varela_autopoiesis_reference
concepts.definition: Maturana + Varela's autopoiesis (1972). Living systems as self-producing. Reference for autopoietic_closure_at_system_scale. The substrate aspires to autopoietic self-maintenance — failure to self-maintain is failure of L6 coordination.

concepts.name: paper1_theorem_root_reference
concepts.definition: Paper 1's Theorem Root — the intended top-level universal coordination theorem. Currently sparse in Jabberwock's vocabulary; this Mt commits to it as the formal target this layer eventually proves.

concepts.name: naming_completes_l6_design
concepts.definition: Meta. Before this Mt, L6 was the top of the runner-design stack but had no composition pattern naming WHAT the coordination layer composes. Now: 10 components + 5 invariants + the explicit connection to Paper 1's Theorem Root. The substrate's top-level regulation surface has a name.

concepts.name: this_mt_closes_the_six_layer_stack
concepts.definition: Meta. With this Mt + drives_estimation_control (L3) + seven_meta_shape_subsystems (L4) + reflective_codegen_axiom3 (L5) + adaptive_tiered_dispatch (L2-dyn) + typed_graph_arena_layout (L1) + executable_memory_lifecycle (shared), ALL SEVEN composition patterns of the runner design are now Mts. The runner-design walk of commit 47b3370 is fully named.

rules.name: essential_variables_must_be_monitored_every_tick
rules.head: Jabberwock's coordination layer is active
rules.body: the essential variables (deadline-meet rate, working set fit, gamma_epoch coherence, drive balance) MUST be sampled every L6 coordination tick. Without continuous monitoring, viability envelope departures are detected only post-failure.

rules.name: cross_layer_signals_use_named_surfaces
rules.head: Jabberwock coordinates across layers
rules.body: layers communicate via named signals (gamma_epoch, hot_counters, drive_state, subsystem_load, code_cache_pressure). Reading another layer's internals is forbidden — destroys coupling discipline + invalidates the composition's design coherence.

rules.name: viability_envelope_breach_triggers_degraded_mode
rules.head: Jabberwock detects an essential variable outside its bounds
rules.body: the substrate must enter degraded mode — reduce drives, increase coordination tick rate, page out cold state, alert reflexes. Continued nominal operation when essential variables are out of bounds violates Ashby + substrate fails silently.

rules.name: second_order_observation_is_complete
rules.head: Jabberwock asks 'what am I doing?'
rules.body: the answer comes entirely from graph introspection — every layer's runtime state is graph-resident. No hidden Rust state. If a question cannot be answered from graph data, the missing state must be EXPOSED (the Mt's invariant on completeness).

rules.name: system_variety_must_match_disturbance_variety
rules.head: Jabberwock encounters a new disturbance class
rules.body: the substrate must add at least one regulator capable of countering it OR formally accept that the new disturbance is outside the viability envelope. Silent toleration violates Ashby + erodes coordination.

rules.name: coordination_latency_must_be_bounded
rules.head: Jabberwock's coordination signal propagates between layers
rules.body: the signal must reach all subscribers within one L2 tick period (100µs default). Larger latency means layers act on stale cross-views + coherence is lost. Use atomics with Release/Acquire pairing for fast propagation.
